payload.abstract: The purpose of this study was to obtain sex- and age-specific reference levels for hearing threshold of normal aging in Koreans and to determine if the rate of change in pure-tone hearing thresholds differed by sex. Subjects were clients who visited the Health Promotion Center, Daegu Fatima Hospital, Daegu, Korea, from January 2004 to April 2010. Pure-tone audiometric measures were obtained from 16,884 subjects who also completed a hearing questionnaire. Data were excluded for the present analyses if the subjects were foreigners, repeated testers, or did not complete the questionnaire. Also excluded were subjects with a positive history of otorrhea for any ear, usage of intravenous antibiotics, diuretics, and chemotherapeutic agents, head injury, job in a noisy environment, and military service. Any subjects with asymmetric hearing results were also excluded. More than a 15 dB difference at 0.5, 1, or 2 kHz was defined as asymmetric hearing. Subjects younger than 18 years were excluded to ensure completion of puberty among female subjects. Because no men were older than 80 years, women older than 80 years were excluded to match the age range between sexes. Finally, 4,084 subjects, 910 men and 3,174 women, were included. As part of the health check, subjects completed continuous pure tone audiometric testing followed by pulsed pure-tone testing. Hearing threshold levels were obtained at six frequencies (0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, and 8 kHz). This dataset provides reference values for age-related hearing loss in a carefully screened normal aging population.
